reflections: Walk me through the facts first — who did what, when, and to whom? Torts turns on the facts before it turns on the rule.
Start with duty. Who was the defendant, and what relationship, if any, did they have to the plaintiff?
Which element are you actually stuck on — duty, breach, cause, or damages? They fail independently.
What would a reasonable person have done differently, and what would that have changed?
Was the harm foreseeable to this defendant at the time they acted?
hints: Florida apportions damages by comparative fault under § 768.81 — a plaintiff's own fault reduces recovery rather than barring it.
Punitive damages must be pleaded with a reasonable evidentiary basis before they can be argued: § 768.72.
A wrongful death claim belongs to the survivors and the estate for their own losses, and is separate from any survival claim: § 768.19.
